Malchiah
mal-kī´ah
n. (several men, including the owner of the dungeon into which Jeremiah was cast; Hebrew Malkiyah)
Hebrew Malkiyah, ‘the LORD is my king’ — from melek, king, with the divine name. The KJV also spells it Malchijah.

Biblical Definition

Malchiah is borne by several men, and two of them stand at opposite ends of the same book. One is Pashur the son of Malchiah, among the princes who heard Jeremiah's preaching and demanded his death, saying that he weakened the hands of the men of war (Jer 38:1). The other gives his name to the pit: “Then took they Jeremiah, and cast him into the dungeon of Malchiah the son of Hammelech, that was in the court of the prison… and in the dungeon there was no water, but mire: so Jeremiah sunk in the mire” (Jer 38:6). A Malchiah of a very different sort appears in Nehemiah: the son of Rechab, ruler of part of Bethhaccerem, who repaired the dung gate and set up its doors, locks and bars (Neh 3:14). The dung gate was the refuse gate of Jerusalem, the least honourable assignment on the wall, and a ruler took it. The name is also in the priestly genealogy of the sons of Levi (1Ch 6:40). All of them are called by a name that confesses the LORD as king; not all of them lived as though He were.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) does not enter Malchiah; the name is fixed by the Hebrew text as, the LORD is my king.

expand to see more

The proper name is not entered in Webster's 1828 dictionary.

MALCHIAH. The name of several men in the Old Testament; also written Malchijah.

The name signifies, Jehovah is my king, from melek, a king.

One Malchiah owned the miry dungeon into which Jeremiah was let down with cords.

Another, the son of Rechab, repaired the dung gate of Jerusalem under Nehemiah.

Key Scripture

Jer 38:1 — "Then Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashur, and Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashur the son of Malchiah, heard the words that Jeremiah had spoken unto all the people, saying,"

Jer 38:6 — "Then took they Jeremiah, and cast him into the dungeon of Malchiah the son of Hammelech, that was in the court of the prison: and they let down Jeremiah with cords. And in the dungeon there was no water, but mire: so Jeremiah sunk in the mire."

Neh 3:14 — "But the dung gate repaired Malchiah the son of Rechab, the ruler of part of Bethhaccerem; he built it, and set up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof."

1Ch 6:40 — "The son of Michael, the son of Baaseiah, the son of Malchiah,"

Modern Corruption

Faithful speech is judged by whether it strengthens morale, the exact charge laid against Jeremiah before he was put in Malchiah's pit.

expand to see more

The princes did not accuse Jeremiah of lying. Their charge was that he weakened the hands of the men of war and sought not the welfare of the people but the hurt — that is, his message was bad for morale, and therefore he had to be silenced. It is a permanently available argument, and its power is that it never has to engage the question of whether the thing said is true. A prophet who is right at the wrong moment is still, on this reasoning, a traitor. Zedekiah, who believed Jeremiah and feared his own princes, gave him up with the most cowardly sentence in the book: he is in your hand, for the king is not he that can do any thing against you.

The principle to recover is that truth is not measured by its effect on confidence. Jeremiah was let down into the mire for saying what God had told him to say, and the word he spoke came true within two years. Set against him is the other Malchiah on the wall in Nehemiah, a ruler who took the dung gate — the refuse gate, the humblest station on the whole circuit — and built it with its doors and locks and bars. Both men are named for the same confession, that the LORD is king. One line of the family owned the pit; another repaired the gate nobody wanted. The name settles nothing; the life shows what it was worth.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Malkiyah (H4441), the LORD is my king; from melek (H4428), king, with Yah, the divine name.

expand to see more

Hebrew Malkiyah (H4441) — Malchiah, also spelled Malchijah; Jeremiah 38:6, Nehemiah 3:14.

Hebrew melek (H4428) — a king; the first element of the name.

Hebrew bor (H953) — a pit, cistern, dungeon; Jeremiah 38:6.

Hebrew tit (H2916) — mire, clay; Jeremiah 38:6, Psalm 40:2.

Hebrew shaar ha-ashpoth — the dung gate, the refuse gate of Jerusalem; Nehemiah 3:14.

Usage

"“The dungeon of Malchiah… there was no water, but mire” — the prophet's pit."

"“The dung gate repaired Malchiah the son of Rechab” — a ruler at the humblest station."

"“He weakeneth the hands of the men of war” — the charge that avoids the question of truth."
